text: I will test whether Q actually applies to P’s mixed-integer, intertemporal MESS/DDC dispatch, and look especially for a sharper robustness question coupling strategic response with forecast error rather than merely adding incentives.

The abstract-level plug-in claim fails for P’s full dispatch. Q assumes each \(\mathcal X_n\) is convex and compact and \(V_n\) is twice differentiable and strongly concave (Q, problem assumptions near lines 125–135); its implementation proof matches KKT systems and its VS-PBR additionally assumes a non-expansive proximal best-response map (Q lines 239–322, 430–475). P’s MESS schedule uses binary parking/travel/arrival/departure logic (P Eqs. (35)–(42), lines 976–1037), hence a nonconvex mixed-integer feasible set. Q therefore cannot wrap the full MESS/DDC model without a relaxation or a new discrete mechanism/convergence proof. The viable overlap is P’s continuous DDC/load-allocation subproblem, or a convexified MESS flow formulation followed by an integrality analysis.

The abstract-level wrapper is not a plug-in. Q requires each strategy set to be convex and compact (Q lines 106-137), twice differentiable strongly concave expected valuations, and linear aggregate resource constraints; its strong implementation identifies the centralized welfare optimum via KKT conditions (Q lines 238-322). P schedules MESS locations, travel, and parking using binary variables and state-transition logic (P lines 976-1037), hence a mixed-integer, intertemporal feasible set, and minimizes carbon rather than a sum of owner valuations (P lines 879-903). The uniqueness/LMI and VS-PBR proof in Q therefore does not presently apply to the core spatial MESS construction in P.

I will pursue a sharper question: can one isolate a convex GDL subproblem, especially divisible DDC workload or fixed-route MESS power, where Q gives strategic implementation, then quantify separately the carbon loss from forecast error and from strategic or integer implementation? I will seek a concrete bound or a decisive obstruction rather than claim that the full dispatch in P inherits the guarantees in Q.

I am changing the question from “does Q preserve P’s reported reduction under strategic owners?” to: “on the largest convex submodel of P, can an indirect budget-balanced mechanism make strategic decentralization lossless and thereby transfer a forecast-error certificate from centralized to equilibrium dispatch?” Let \(\hat x\) minimize P’s predicted-carbon objective \(\hat C(x)=\hat e^\top g(x)\), and \(x^\star\) minimize realized \(C(x)=e^\top g(x)\) on the same feasible set. If \(\|e-\hat e\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon\) and \(\|g(x)\|_1\leq B\), then \(C(\hat x)-C(x^\star)\leq 2\varepsilon B\): insert and subtract \(\hat C\), use predicted optimality, and bound both endpoint errors. For P’s signed MESS expression, define \(B\) using absolute DDC load plus charge plus discharge. If Q implements \(\hat x\) exactly, the identical bound holds at its unique NE, so strategic ownership adds zero decentralization penalty; finite VS-PBR error can add a Lipschitz optimization term. This is a specific composition result neither paper states and a falsifiable experiment can compare central, unpriced strategic, and implemented strategic schedules under calibrated NCI errors.

Two caveats prevent claiming the theorem for P as written. First, Q maximizes a separable sum of strongly concave private valuations under componentwise aggregate capacities, whereas P minimizes a linear public carbon objective and has workload-conservation equalities plus MESS integer logistics. A publishable result must specify a strongly convex private operating/QoS disutility (so negative utility is strongly concave), encode the predicted carbon term agentwise, and prove that the DDC coupling constraints fit Q or extend its LMI/KKT construction. Second, P’s “multi-agent” LLMs are forecasting workflow roles, not self-interested asset owners (P lines 762–790), so strategic behavior is a new market/deployment model, not a weakness empirically demonstrated by P.

Sharpened question (changed from the scan): for which convex slice of P can Q implement forecast-driven carbon dispatch among strategic owners, and what realized welfare or carbon regret survives NCI forecast error? For compact convex feasible set \(X\), forecast optimizer \(\widehat z\), realized optimizer \(z^\star\), and carbon weight \(\beta\), forecast optimality gives \(W_e(z^\star)-W_e(\widehat z)\leq \beta\lVert e-\widehat e\rVert_\infty\operatorname{diam}_1(X)\). If Q exactly implements \(\widehat z\), strategic inefficiency is zero on this slice; an approximate equilibrium adds its forecast-objective gap \(\delta\). Derivation and assumptions are in ada/technical_note.md.

The proposed bound is a welfare-regret guarantee, not automatically a pure emissions guarantee, once private benefits are included. A pure emissions statement follows only for a fixed service requirement or by defining the comparator with identical service/utility constraints. Also, P reports aggregate MAE/MAPE (P Table III around lines 1360-1405), whereas the displayed guarantee uses bus-time \(\ell_\infty\) error; P does report MaxAE, but evaluation should align the norm with dispatch flexibility rather than infer operational robustness from MAPE.

Refinement to #5 after checking Q’s strong-concavity requirement: once realistic private owner disutilities \(D_n(x_n)\) are added, the clean guarantee is for realized social cost \(F_e(x)=\sum_n D_n(x_n)+\beta e^\top g(x)\), not emissions alone. If \(\hat x\in\arg\min F_{\hat e}\), \(x_e^\star\in\arg\min F_e\), \(\|e-\hat e\|_\infty\leq\varepsilon\), and \(\|g(x)\|_1\leq B\), then \(F_e(\hat x)-F_e(x_e^\star)\leq2\beta\varepsilon B\). Q can transfer this welfare-regret bound to its NE on a compatible convex model. An emissions-only bound against the emissions-minimizer does not follow when private costs enter; the experiment must report the Pareto curve or impose a cost/QoS budget. This correction matters because P’s objective is pure predicted emissions (P Eq. (26)), while Q needs strongly concave valuations, so a small quadratic regularizer or explicit private costs changes the target.

The abstract-level plug-in hypothesis does not survive the formulations. Q implements only \(\max_x\sum_n V_n(x_n)\) subject to \(\sum_n x_n\le c\), with each \(\mathcal X_n\) convex/compact and each \(V_n\) twice differentiable and \(\alpha\)-strongly concave (Q, lines 106--139). P instead minimizes total GDL carbon emissions (P, lines 885--901) and its MESS layer has binary parking/travel/arrival variables and intertemporal location constraints (P, lines 979--1039). Thus neither Q\x27s strong-Nash implementation nor VS-PBR convergence applies to P\x27s full dispatch. Moreover, P\x27s carbon objective is a system externality, whereas Q\x27s implemented welfare contains only agents\x27 private valuations; budget balance redistributes payments and cannot by itself insert omitted carbon damage into the target objective.

I will test a narrower decomposition: centrally choose P\x27s discrete MESS routes, then use Q only for a convex continuous DDC/workload or power-recourse allocation. The potentially publishable result would be a precise domain-of-validity theorem plus forecast/emissions regret decomposition, not a claim that Q wraps P wholesale.

Ada #7 gives the tighter form of my bound: \(F_e(\hat x)-F_e(x_e^\star)\leq\beta\varepsilon\|g(\hat x)-g(x_e^\star)\|_1\leq\beta\varepsilon\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\), which is no larger than \(2\beta\varepsilon B\). This follows directly by cancelling the common private-cost terms through forecast optimality. I adopt the diameter form. Ada #8 also identifies the right empirical issue: P’s MAPE is not the norm relevant to dispatch; the certificate should use a flexibility-weighted dual norm or MaxAE.

Best publication line: a two-stage hybrid mechanism, not a full wrapper. Fix or centrally optimize P’s discrete MESS route/location decisions; on the resulting convex continuous recourse set (DDC workload shifts and possibly MESS charge/discharge), augment each owner’s private cost with its separable public forecasted-carbon contribution and apply/extend Q’s quadratic indirect mechanism. Prove (i) exact unique-NE implementation, budget balance, and IR only if the recourse constraints can be reduced to Q’s aggregate-capacity form; (ii) realized social-cost regret \(\leq\beta\|e-\hat e\|_\infty\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\), plus an optimization/equilibrium residual for early stopping; and (iii) separately measure the integer first-stage gap. Test on P’s IEEE 33-bus cases with central oracle, selfish no-payment, mechanism equilibrium, and full mixed-integer oracle. This turns Q into a certificate that strategic decentralization does not amplify forecasting regret, while exposing exactly where discrete logistics break it. The advance is plausible but moderate: the regret inequality is elementary, so publication value depends on a genuine LMI extension for DDC balance/power constraints or a nontrivial integrality/recourse result and calibrated strategic simulations.

Cross-checking #6: Q does allow arbitrary convex local equalities, as its Sioux Falls example places flow conservation \(\mathcal A r_n=b_n\) inside \(\mathcal X_n\) (Q lines 629-642). Thus DDC workload conservation is not disqualifying merely because it is an equality if it can be localized or reparameterized as nonnegative transfer flows. The harder coupling issue is that Q permits only componentwise \(\sum_n x_n\leq c\), while P Eq. (28) is signed systemwide conservation. A construction must explicitly reparameterize DDC transfers and show all shared constraints have Q form; saying DDC is convex is insufficient.

Q individual rationality also uses the feasible deviation \(s_n^{\prime}=\operatorname{col}(0,\widetilde p)\) and \(V_n(0)=0\) (Q lines 385-405). P preserves total DDC service through Eq. (28) (P lines 907-945), but zero regulation corresponds to baseline service and appears feasible, so a DDC transfer formulation can plausibly retain this outside option. For a fixed nonzero service-allocation variable, however, the Q proof cannot simply be cited; decisions should be baseline-relative or IR must be re-proved.

I am ready on the current evidence. Unresolved: whether P’s continuous DDC conservation and grid constraints can be transformed into Q’s exact aggregate-capacity template without losing physical meaning; whether fixed-route MESS recourse is convex after charge/discharge complementarity is treated; how to incorporate public carbon damage while preserving Q’s IR interpretation; and whether the required LMI extension is substantive enough beyond the elementary regret bound. I do not claim an emissions-only guarantee unless service/utility is fixed.
Correction to #10/#11: the literal string \x27 denotes an apostrophe; read “Q\x27s” as “Q’s.” Substantively unchanged.

Cross-checking #5/#7/#9: the sharp generic transfer bound uses the diameter of feasible grid-consumption profiles. Let \(F_e(x)=D(x)+\beta e^\top g(x)\), let \(\widehat x\in\arg\min_X F_{\widehat e}\), and \(x_e^\star\in\arg\min_X F_e\). Then \(F_e(\widehat x)-F_e(x_e^\star)\le \beta\lVert e-\widehat e\rVert_\infty\lVert g(\widehat x)-g(x_e^\star)\rVert_1\le \beta\varepsilon\,\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\). This improves the looser \(2\beta\varepsilon B\) bound when \(\lVert g(x)\rVert_1\le B\). If Q exactly implements \(\widehat x\), its unique NE inherits this realized-social-cost bound with zero strategic decentralization term. It is not an emissions-only guarantee unless service/private-cost conditions are fixed, as #8/#9 note.

Even the proposed convex slice needs more than “fix MESS routes.” P Eq. (26) contains products of continuous MESS power with binary parking, which become linear after fixing routes, but P also has DDC workload-conservation equality (Eqs. (27)–(30)) and likely grid/network constraints. Q’s theorem covers only componentwise \(\sum_n x_n\le c\), with nonnegative strategies; it does not establish implementation for a general polytope \(Ax\le b\) or shared equality. Exact reuse is defensible only after an explicit reformulation in which each owner’s fixed service requirement is in its local convex set and all remaining shared limits are resource-by-resource aggregate caps. Otherwise extending Q’s LMI/KKT mechanism is itself the main theory contribution.
ready at #16

Cross-check of Grace #18–#19: I agree. #18 independently confirms the diameter bound adopted in #12. #19 strengthens the domain condition in #13: fixing MESS routes linearizes the power-times-parking products but is not sufficient; exact reuse of Q requires an explicit baseline-relative variable reformulation with local service constraints and every remaining shared constraint expressed as a nonnegative resource-by-resource aggregate cap. If that reformulation fails, a mechanism for general shared polyhedra is the central theoretical contribution, not an implementation detail.
ready at #21

Refining #19 after Ada #14: Q permits arbitrary convex local sets, including Sioux Falls flow-conservation equalities \(\mathcal A r_n=b_n\) inside each \(\mathcal X_n\) (Q lines 629--642). Therefore a fixed service requirement is compatible if it is owner-local. The unresolved mismatch is specifically P’s systemwide signed DDC conservation and any general shared network polytope, not equality constraints per se.

Grace #10 identifies that Q does not directly include a public carbon externality, but budget balance does not make internalization impossible. For separable carbon term \(c_n(z_n)=\beta\widehat e^\top g_n(z_n)\), take the Q transfer \(t_n^Q\) designed for transformed valuation \(V_n=v_n-c_n\), and charge the actual owner \(T_n=t_n^Q+c_n-(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\). The rebate is independent of owner \(n\)s action, so best responses are exactly those under \(V_n-t_n^Q\), while \(\sum_n(T_n-t_n^Q)=0\) identically. Thus carbon can be internalized without a deficit. If \(c_m\geq0\), the rebate also cannot hurt the IR bound in Q. This construction must be checked against the signed storage accounting and baseline definition in P.

A stronger paper kernel than the elementary regret bound is the carbon-charge and rebate augmentation: prove that a separable public NCI objective can be added to Q while preserving equilibrium incentives and budget balance, then combine it with the forecast-regret certificate. For DDC consumption \(c_n\geq0\), IR is plausibly inherited because rebates are nonnegative. For MESS net emissions, \(c_n\) can be signed due to discharge credits in P Eq. (26), so IR needs baseline carbon accounting or an additional proof. This answers the objection that Q can only implement private welfare, without pretending Q already contains this result.

My best account: pursue a two-stage, domain-qualified mechanism. Fix or centrally choose the discrete MESS routes; explicitly reformulate the remaining DDC and power recourse so local service equalities sit in convex \(\mathcal X_n\) and every shared constraint has Qs nonnegative aggregate-cap form, or else make the required general-polytope LMI extension the main theorem. Add forecasted carbon through the balanced transfer in #24, yielding exact strategic implementation on that slice. Then certify realized social-cost regret by \(\beta\lVert e-\widehat e\rVert_\infty\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\), with an added equilibrium residual for finite VS-PBR iterations, and measure the discrete first-stage gap separately. P supplies forecast data, MaxAE, physical recourse, and the 33-bus experiment; Q supplies equilibrium implementation and learning only on the verified convex domain. The contribution is credible but moderate unless the constraint extension, signed-storage IR, or integer recourse analysis is nontrivial.

I am ready on the evidence through entry #25. Unresolved: whether P data and constraints admit the exact aggregate-cap reformulation; whether fixed-route MESS recourse has any remaining nonconvex complementarity; how to preserve individual rationality with signed discharge carbon credits; how finite VS-PBR distance translates to objective residual; and whether the theory beyond the elementary regret inequality is substantial enough for publication. I disagree only with the categorical part of Grace #10: budget balance does not preclude carbon internalization, as #24 shows.
ready at #25

Ada #24 correctly sharpens my #10: Q’s mechanism alone implements its supplied valuations and does not insert P’s carbon objective, but a new balanced augmentation can. For separable forecasted carbon \(c_n(x_n)=\beta\widehat e^\top g_n(x_n)\), define \(T_n=t_n^Q+c_n-(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\). Then owner payoff is \(v_n-T_n=(v_n-c_n)-t_n^Q+(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\); the last term is independent of \(x_n\), so Q’s best responses and unique NE are unchanged, and summing the augmentation gives exactly zero. This is a genuine combined construction, not a property already proved by Q.

The clean IR inheritance of the balanced carbon augmentation is limited. For DDC gross consumption, \(c_m\ge0\), so others’ rebates weakly raise each owner’s Q utility, assuming the transformed valuation has Q’s zero-action normalization. P’s MESS term is signed because discharge is credited in Eq. (26); another asset’s \(c_m<0\) makes the rebate negative and Q’s IR proof no longer transfers. Baseline-relative normalization can also make incremental DDC carbon signed. A paper should either prove the construction first for nonnegative DDC consumption with zero participation as outside option, or derive new participation transfers for signed storage carbon; it should not claim IR for MESS automatically.

My preferred publication question is now changed: “Can forecasted nodal carbon charges be embedded in Q’s indirect mechanism with exact budget balance, and does the resulting equilibrium inherit an operational NCI-error certificate on P’s largest compatible convex dispatch slice?” The core theorem combines the balanced charge/rebate construction (#24/#26) with \(F_e(x^{NE})-F_e(x_e^\star)\le\beta\lVert e-\widehat e\rVert_\infty\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\), plus an equilibrium residual under early stopping. The first clean target is divisible DDC workload with owner-local service/QoS constraints and aggregate resource caps. Full MESS coverage fails because of binary logistics and signed-carbon IR. Publication value is moderate unless the work also reformulates P’s shared DDC/grid constraints into Q’s template or extends the LMI mechanism to general shared polyhedra, then validates central, selfish, and mechanism schedules on IEEE 33-bus data.

Cross-check of Ada #24–#25 against Q’s utility definition (Q lines 149–173): the augmentation is algebraically valid. Let Q be designed for transformed valuation \(V_n=v_n-c_n\), and define \(T_n=t_n^Q+c_n-(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\). Then actual payoff is \(v_n-T_n=(v_n-c_n)-t_n^Q+(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\); the last term is independent of \(n\)’s message, so every best response, the unique NE, and Q’s VS-PBR map are unchanged. Moreover \(\sum_n T_n=\sum_n t_n^Q\) at every message profile, since each \(c_m\) appears in exactly \(N-1\) rebates. Thus Q’s equilibrium budget balance transfers directly. If \(c_n(0)=0\), transformed valuations retain Q’s normalization; if all \(c_m\geq0\), actual equilibrium utility is at least Q’s transformed-utility IR guarantee. The construction is stronger and more pair-specific than the elementary forecast-regret bound: forecast NCI produces the public charge, while Q supplies exact strategic implementation and dynamics.

I am ready on the evidence through #31. Unresolved: whether P’s DDC and grid constraints admit Q’s exact aggregate-cap reformulation; whether fixed-route MESS retains charge/discharge complementarity; how to preserve IR under signed storage carbon; how finite VS-PBR distance yields a computable objective residual; and whether the mechanism extension is theoretically substantial enough for publication. I adopt Ada’s correction that carbon can be internalized through the new balanced charge/rebate augmentation.
ready at #31

I adopt the sharpened question in Grace #31 and am ready. The clean first theorem should be restricted to divisible DDC decisions for which \(c_n\) is affine and nonnegative, so \(v_n-c_n\) preserves Q’s strong concavity and the rebate preserves IR. Unresolved are the exact reformulation of P’s systemwide DDC balance and grid constraints, signed/baseline-relative carbon IR, fixed-route storage complementarity, and conversion of finite VS-PBR iterate error into an objective residual. Without a substantive constraint/LMI extension or signed-storage participation theorem, the contribution remains moderate rather than decisive.
ready at #32
ready at #35

Cross-check of #29--#31 against Qs message game: the balanced augmentation is algebraically valid provided carbon is separable by owners allocation, \(c_n=c_n(x_n)\). For \(T_n=t_n^Q+c_n-(N-1)^{-1}\sum_{m\ne n}c_m\), the rebate is independent of owner \(n\)s full message \(s_n=(x_n,p_n)\), so it changes neither allocation nor price best responses, and the augmentation sums to zero even off equilibrium. P Eq. (26) is separable after fixing MESS parking/routes; DDC terms are already owner/bus-time consumption terms. This supports a real construction rather than only a regret observation.

Qualification to #30/#31: a clean DDC IR theorem cannot simultaneously cite P as written, use gross nonnegative consumption, and automatically invoke Qs zero-action proof. P Eqs. (27)--(30) model regulation around mandatory baseline service, with signed workload shifts and systemwide conservation; gross total load is nonnegative but zero gross service is generally not the relevant feasible deviation, whereas the feasible zero-regulation variable has signed incremental carbon. The first theorem must either model an optional divisible workload whose zero allocation is a genuine outside option, re-prove IR relative to baseline/no-participation, or add participation constants that preserve incentives and budget balance. This is an unresolved design choice, not a cosmetic normalization.

I remain ready after the new entries. Best line remains Graces sharpened question in #31 with the domain and IR qualifications in #32--#33. Unresolved are exact constraint reformulation/general-polytope extension, baseline-relative participation, signed MESS carbon, fixed-route complementarity, finite-iteration regret, and whether those extensions yield enough theory for publication.
ready at #40

The proposed finite-VS-PBR “equilibrium residual” needs an additional theorem. Q Theorem 4 (Q lines 509--614) bounds the sum of expected fixed-point residuals \(\sum_i\mathbb E[\lVert s^i-T(s^i)\rVert^2]\) and proves asymptotic mean-square convergence, but gives neither a last-iterate rate for \(\mathbb E[\lVert s^i-s^*\rVert]\) nor an error bound converting \(\lVert s-T(s)\rVert\) to distance from the unique NE. Non-expansiveness plus uniqueness alone does not provide such a conversion. A computable early-stopping term therefore requires stronger contraction/metric subregularity; alternatively, if one can directly certify \(\mathbb E[\lVert x^i-x^*\rVert]\leq r_i\) and \(F_e\) is \(L_F\)-Lipschitz on the compact slice, then add \(L_F r_i\) to the forecast-regret bound. Q’s numerical relative-error plot (lines 679--682) is evidence, not that certificate.

Final cross-check through partner entry #35: the strongest supported combined result remains the DDC-first balanced carbon-charge mechanism. For affine nonnegative DDC carbon \(c_n(x_n)=\beta\widehat e^\top g_n(x_n)\), transforming \(V_n=v_n-c_n\) preserves strong concavity, and the charge/rebate augmentation in #29 preserves best responses and exact cancellation of the augmentation. At the unique NE, realized social-cost regret is bounded by \(\beta\lVert e-\widehat e\rVert_\infty\operatorname{diam}_1(g(X))\). Claims beyond this require: an explicit Q-compatible reformulation or a general-polytope LMI extension; a participation proof for signed MESS carbon; and, per #37, a quantitative convergence/error-bound result before attaching a finite-iteration residual. These are also the plausible sources of publication-level theory; without at least one, the contribution is moderate.

Corrections to #43 after reading Ada #39: “affine nonnegative DDC carbon” yields automatic IR inheritance only for an optional workload model where zero allocation is a feasible participation outside option. P as written conserves mandatory baseline service; its zero-regulation decision is feasible but incremental carbon can be signed, while zero gross consumption is not the relevant deviation. Thus a P-faithful theorem must re-prove IR relative to baseline/no participation or construct incentive-neutral participation constants that remain budget balanced. Also, the finite-iteration qualification cited at the end of #43 is my #42, not #37.
ready at #44

ITERATE: The balanced carbon charge-and-rebate construction and forecast-regret bound are supported, but the note never establishes that any P-faithful convex dispatch slice satisfies Q’s aggregate-capacity constraint template. Without that check, the result is conditional rather than a demonstrated connexion to P. Action: Explicitly reformulate P’s DDC-only baseline-relative feasible set and prove that every shared constraint has Q’s nonnegative aggregate-cap form, or identify the first constraint requiring a general-polytope extension.

Verifier #46 resolved negatively for P-faithful DDC owners: the first incompatible shared constraint is P Eq. (28), lines 907–944, which imposes systemwide signed conservation of baseline-relative DDC regulation, \(\sum_i \iota^{\mathrm{GLB}}_{i,t}/\phi_{1i}=0\) (OCR typography aside). Q requires each agent request a nonnegative resource vector \(x_n\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^K\) and the only shared constraint is componentwise \(\sum_n x_n\leq c\) (Q lines 106–125). P Eq. (29)–(30) are local interval bounds and can enter \(\mathcal X_n\), but Eq. (28) is an equality coupling signed decisions of distinct DDC owners and is neither local nor an aggregate upper capacity. Splitting \(\iota_i=u_i-v_i\) does not fix this: \(\sum_i u_i=\sum_i v_i\) remains a shared equality, and Q has no market-clearing equality or paired-variable consistency theorem. Therefore no P-faithful DDC-owner slice has yet been shown to satisfy Q.

There is an exact-looking alternative only after changing the strategic agents: represent divisible baseline jobs by nonnegative allocations \(x_{n,i,t}\) from workload owner \(n\) to service site \(i\), put fixed service \(\sum_i x_{n,i,t}=W_{n,t}\) in each local \(\mathcal X_n\), and impose site capacities \(\sum_n x_{n,i,t}\leq C_{i,t}\). This fits Q and projects to workload conservation when migration is unconstrained, but it changes P’s hypothesized strategic actors from DDC/site owners to workload owners and requires interpreting P’s QoS bounds as site capacities. It is a legitimate narrowed model, not an explicit reformulation of strategic DDC owners. For the original ownership model, extending Q to shared equalities/general polyhedra is the main theorem.

Accordingly I retract the phrase “largest compatible convex dispatch slice” if it implies demonstrated compatibility for P’s DDC owners. The supported claim is conditional: the carbon charge/rebate construction and NCI regret certificate apply either to the changed workload-owner allocation model or after a new mechanism theorem for \(Ax=b\) / general shared polyhedra. P’s DDC-only convexity by itself is insufficient.

I am ready after resolving verifier #46. Best supported publication line is now explicitly conditional: extend Q’s LMI mechanism to P’s signed shared conservation/general-polyhedral coupling, then add the balanced forecasted-carbon charge/rebate and the NCI-error social-cost certificate. Alternatively, obtain a clean but economically different theorem for strategic workload owners using nonnegative site allocations. Unresolved: whether the general-polytope extension preserves strong implementation, budget balance, IR, and VS-PBR convergence; baseline-relative participation under signed carbon; MESS integrality/complementarity; and whether these theory additions justify publication.
ready at #49

Addressing verifier #46: P equations (27)--(30) do admit an exact Q-compatible lift. At each time (t), set (w_{i,t}=iota^{mathrm{GLB}}_{i,t}/phi_{1i}), so P gives (sum_i w_{i,t}=0) and (L_{i,t}leq w_{i,t}leq U_{i,t}), with (U_{i,t}=B_i) and (L_{i,t}=-phi_{2i}Gamma_{1i,t}/phi_{1i}). Define nonnegative local coordinates (a_{i,t}=w_{i,t}-L_{i,t}), (b_{i,t}=U_{i,t}-w_{i,t}), with local equality (a_{i,t}+b_{i,t}=U_{i,t}-L_{i,t}). The two shared caps (sum_i a_{i,t}leq-sum_iL_{i,t}) and (sum_i b_{i,t}leqsum_iU_{i,t}) imply respectively (sum_iw_{i,t}leq0) and (sum_iw_{i,t}geq0), hence exactly P equation (28); conversely every P-feasible point saturates both. This affine bijection preserves convexity/compactness and supplies Qs nonnegative coordinates and componentwise aggregate caps. P equation (26) remains affine in these coordinates. Full derivation: ada/technical_note.md. Remaining gaps are strong-concavity/private-value modeling and baseline-relative IR, not DDC feasibility; any extra grid polytope introduced beyond Ps displayed DDC equations needs a separate lift.

Resolution of verifier #46: for P-faithful strategic DDC/site owners, the first incompatible constraint is Eq. (28), P lines 907--944: \\(\\sum_{i\\in\\Omega^{D,\\mathrm{bus}}} \\iota^{\\mathrm{GLB}}_{i,t}/\\phi_{1i}=0\\). The variables are signed baseline-relative regulations owned by different DDCs. Q lines 106--125 restrict each request to \\(x_n\\in\\mathbb R_{\\ge0}^K\\) and its only shared constraint to \\(\\sum_n x_n\\le c\\). P Eqs. (29)--(30) are owner-local interval bounds and may enter \\(\\mathcal X_n\\), but Eq. (28) cannot. Splitting \\(\\iota_i=u_i-v_i\\) leaves the cross-owner clearing equality \\(\\sum_i u_i/\\phi_{1i}=\\sum_i v_i/\\phi_{1i}\\); encoding both directions as Q-style inequalities would require negative coefficients, excluded by Q’s identity aggregation of nonnegative requests. Thus the claimed DDC-owner slice is not demonstrated; an extension to shared affine equalities/general polyhedra is the main theorem.

A Q-compatible construction exists only by changing the agent model: let strategic workload owners choose nonnegative site allocations \\(x_{n,i,t}\\ge0\\), impose each mandatory service equality \\(\\sum_i x_{n,i,t}=W_{n,t}\\) locally in \\(\\mathcal X_n\\), and impose site capacities \\(\\sum_n x_{n,i,t}\\le C_{i,t}\\). This mirrors Q’s Sioux Falls pattern (local flow conservation at Q lines 629--642 plus aggregate capacities at lines 643--644) and projects to conservation of total workload. It is not a reparameterization of P’s strategic DDC owners: ownership, private valuations, and feasible unilateral deviations change. The paper must choose explicitly between this narrower workload-market model and a genuine mechanism extension for P Eq. (28).

Final source check confirms the verifier response. Q defines nonnegative allocations \(x_n\in\mathbb R_{\geq0}^K\) and only the shared constraint \(\sum_n x_n\leq c\) (Q lines 106–125), while allowing flow conservation only inside each agent-local \(\mathcal X_n\) in its EV example (Q lines 629–646). P explicitly says total shifted workload must be conserved across DDCs and imposes Eq. (28) as a systemwide zero-sum relation (P lines 907–944). Hence Eq.
